items.title: Adrian Cunningham interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 31, 2021
items.q: Miles Davis can't even play the trumpet you know? So what the hell is going on?

ctx.x: It’s interesting that you chose, maybe it’s because of your father but the era of jazz, those two tunes that you played, because I think nowadays, or even at that same time in the States if teenagers got together to play a couple of tunes they’re more likely to be playing John Coltrane or even more current, Michael Brecker or something. So my question is, what was the attitude or thinking about jazz in Australia at that time? Was there more interest in the classic early jazz?

There are a few camps, especially in Sydney. Sydney and Melbourne are quite different flavors. I think Melbourne is more artistically orientated, cultural, it has more European influences, it’s a little hipper dare I say. Sydney is a little more, well there’s just less culture in the same way. Like my father who loved football, I always said if I could figure out a way to play the saxophone and kick a football at the same time I’d be a millionaire. So I think it was something that was I was in somewhat of a…

two of us — he was a trombone player — the two of us had a real connection. Then we got other buddies who happened to be playing instruments at the school and kind of dragged them along you know, an electric bass player, we got him playing 1 – 5 – 1. So we kind of worked it out from there and we just got it together. So I think it was just a lack of other influences from the outside, that we just kind of got together with our own thing. And I do remember being about 16 or 17 with that same buddy, the trombone…
